claims.text: POST /api/v1/orders is [Authorize]; Create reads the customer id from the token's sub claim (JwtRegisteredClaimNames.Sub), and CreateOrderRequest has only Items (productId, quantity, unitPriceVnd).
A successful create answers 201 with the new order as JSON (id, customerId, status, placedAt, items); a newly placed order has status "new".
The client cannot change a claim in the token without the signature check failing, so the API rejects such a token.

In Đơn Hàng, POST /api/v1/orders can answer 401 (no or expired token), 400 (ArgumentException, e.g. no items) and 500 (any other unhandled exception, e.g. database down), the last two as Problem Details.

claims.text: ApiClient.createOrder posts {"items": [...]} built with OrderItemRequest.toJson to $baseUrl/orders with _headers; only 201 is success, parsed with OrderResult.fromJson (id, status); any other status throws Exception('failed to create order (<status>)') without reading the body.

_placeOrder orders product 1 (the keyboard) x1 at 1250000, its seeded price; sets _loading first; shows 'Order <id> placed, status <status>' or 'Failed: $e'; finally resets _loading. onPressed is null while _loading, with a spinner.

With the db container stopped, POST /api/v1/orders with a valid token answers 500 with a Problem Details body (detail "something went wrong") that the browser can read, and the screen shows "Failed: Exception: failed to create order (500)".

claims.text: Different failure statuses ask different actions of the user (sign in again, change the order, try later); one generic message leaves them guessing.

The authentication middleware runs for every request and records the caller from a valid Bearer token; on an [Authorize] endpoint, authorization answers 401 before the action runs when there is no valid caller.
